subject: Architecture
title: Curtain Walls: Skin of Glass
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Curtain Walls: Skin of Glass.

hook.text: Skyscraper walls don't hold anything up. They're just glass curtains hung on the steel skeleton.

buildup.text: Curtain wall systems are assembled from prefabricated panels — glass, aluminum frames, and sealant.

discovery.text: Modern glass can block heat while staying transparent. Low-e coatings reflect infrared light outward.

twist.text: Early curtain walls leaked badly. The John Hancock Tower in Boston dropped glass panels onto the street.

climax.text: Today's unitized curtain walls are factory-sealed and tested to withstand hurricane-force winds.

punchline.text: The walls do nothing structural. They do everything else.

quiz.question: What happened to the John Hancock Tower's curtain wall?
options: It turned opaque in cold weather
Glass panels fell off and dropped onto the street
Wind caused the entire facade to bulge outward

details.summary: Curtain walls are non-structural glass facades hung on the exterior of a building's frame like a curtain. They keep weather out without bearing structural loads, enabling the transparent glass towers that define modern city skylines from New York to Shanghai.
details.whyItMatters: Curtain walls transformed architecture's visual language. By separating the building's skin from its structure, they created the glass-and-steel aesthetic that dominates modern cities and redefined how buildings interact with light.
takeaways: Curtain walls are non-structural, hung on the building frame
They enable fully glazed facades without load-bearing walls
The technology defines the appearance of modern city skylines

faq.question: How does a curtain wall stay attached to the building?
faq.answer: Metal anchors connect the curtain wall panels to the structural frame at each floor level. The connections allow slight movement for thermal expansion and wind deflection. Each panel is sealed with gaskets and sealant to prevent water and air infiltration.

faq.question: Are curtain walls energy efficient?
faq.answer: Early curtain walls were not — single-pane glass lost heat rapidly. Modern versions use double or triple glazing, low-emissivity coatings, argon gas fills, and automated shading. High-performance curtain walls can now match or exceed the thermal performance of insulated solid walls.
